title: Refining and Reusing Annotation Guidelines for LLM Annotation

model.params_source: paper Sec. 4.3 (gpt-5-2025-08-07, reasoning_effort in {low, high} evaluated in Table 2) and the released OpenAIProvider (src/llm_guideline_moderation/providers/openai.py: reasoning_effort=None, i.e. no effort field is sent and the API default 'medium' applies; max_output_tokens=12000; temperature unset). Table 1's rows are therefore most plausibly the default-effort run. Runs so far: high (2026-09-20, 97 of 113 replies empty under the 12,000-token limit; archived at runs/tierb/W7162149911_v1_effort_high_12k/), low (2026-09-20, F1 0.287; archived at runs/tierb/W7162149911_v2_effort_low_12k/); this run uses medium as the best-evidence setting.
model.params_source_v1: paper Sec. 4.3 (gpt-5-2025-08-07 with reasoning_effort in {low, high}; Table 1 is the reasoning variant, i.e. high - its G column 0.73 equals the 'Reason' cell of Table 2) and the released OpenAIProvider (max_output_tokens 12000, temperature left unset because GPT-5 does not support it)

task.subset_rule: paper-defined split: the NCBI Disease development split used in full as the evaluation set (100 documents, 791 gold entities; Sec. 4.2). Canonical medium run (2026-09-21): the first 49 documents in file order, where the $15 cap stopped the run (48 documents with all three seeds); the archived low run covers all 100
task.approximation: The runner sends the prompt as a chat completion without response_format={'type':'json_object'} (the runner drops response_format for reasoning models); the paper's provider sets it together with the JSON-mode system message, which is kept. Span realignment is a simplified version of the repo's align_annotations (exact offsets first, otherwise the nearest occurrence of the returned span text). Strict-match scoring is re-implemented (exact begin/end/label, one-to-one) instead of calling the authors' PubAnnotation evaluator with soft_match 0.

prompt.system: You are a helpful assistant that outputs valid json. Always respond with a JSON object.
prompt.user_template:
You are an expert AI for text annotation. Your task is to annotate all entities from the provided text based on a strict schema and guidelines.

**ENTITY SCHEMA:**
- SpecificDisease
- DiseaseClass
- Modifier
- CompositeMention

**HIGH-LEVEL INSTRUCTIONS:**
Follow the provided guidelines exactly.

**ANNOTATION RULES:**
- Output MUST be a valid JSON object with a single key "annotations".
- "annotations" MUST be an array of objects following this JSON schema:
  {
  "start": integer,
  "end": integer,
  "text": string,
  "entity": string,
  "rationale": string,
  "guideline_section": string
}
- Every annotation MUST include a meaningful "rationale" and cite the corresponding "guideline_section".
- If no entities are found, return {"annotations": []}
- Spans must match the original text exactly. Do not alter spacing, casing, or punctuation.

**ANNOTATION GUIDELINES:**
(no guidelines provided)

**TEXT TO ANNOTATE:**
---
{input_text}
---

Provide your response as a single JSON object.
prompt.few_shot: none (simple prompting / prompt-only baseline, column S of Table 1)
prompt.source_location: Figure 5a (prompt template); the slot fillers for the prompt-only condition come from the released code of the same paper (prompts.py 'annotate_with_guidelines', pipeline.annotate_with_guidelines defaults, prompt_utils.generate_schema_parts, providers/_shared.JSON_MODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, data/schemas/ncbi_entities.schema.json)
prompt.verbatim: full - the paper prints the template with the slots {{entitySchema}} / {{guidelines}} / {{jsonSchema}} / {{inputText}}; the slots are filled with the released code's own defaults: entity schema = the four NCBI labels one per line, guidelines = '(no guidelines provided)' (prompt-only), high-level instructions = 'Follow the provided guidelines exactly.', JSON schema = the six-field object with rationale and guideline_section, plus the matching rationale instruction. The markdown bold markers of the code template are kept; the figure renders them as plain headings.

output.postprocess: hook parse(): strip an optional ```json fence, json.loads, take obj['annotations'], keep entries with a known label, realign offsets to the document text, return the set of (begin, end, label) triples
output.parse_paper: the released code parses the reply with json.loads and reads the key 'annotations', then calls align_annotations(text, ...)

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: strict-match micro F1 over all 100 documents: a prediction counts as a true positive when its begin, end and entity label equal a gold denotation's (one-to-one); P = TP/#pred, R = TP/#gold (791), F1 = 2PR/(P+R)
metric.original_location: Table 1, block NCBI (791), row GPT-5, column group S (simple prompting): P 0.45, R 0.48, F1 0.46, TP 378
metric.bootstrap_unit: document (set-level resample: micro F1 recomputed on resampled documents)

cost.prepare_note: runner --prepare --dry-run --cap 20 on 2026-09-19: 100 items x 3 seeds = 300 calls, prepare estimate $2.39 (120-token json guess + 600 reasoning tokens), dry-run upper bound $36.23 (all 12,000 completion tokens used). est_usd is the middle case, about 2,500 output tokens per reply.
cost.repair_note: third run 2026-09-21: reasoning_effort medium, 100 documents x 3 seeds = 300 calls, max_output_tokens 12000 as released; expected $10-15, cap $15. Actual: about $0.10 per call (median 10,360 completion tokens, most of them reasoning), stopped at the cap after 145 calls / 49 documents, $15.25

open_points: The paper prints the template but not the slot fillers; the values above are the released repository's defaults. In particular the prompt-only condition is assumed to fill {{guidelines}} with the code's fallback '(no guidelines provided)' and to keep the rationale / guideline_section fields of the default OutputConfiguration (include_rationale and include_guideline_section both True in annotate_pubannotation_directory). A different OutputConfiguration would change the prompt slightly.

Table 1 does not name the reasoning_effort of its rows; high is inferred from Table 2 (the 'Reason' column equals the Table 1 G value 0.73 for NCBI GPT). If Table 1's S column were the low-effort run, the baseline would be a different number (Table 2 gives only the G-column pair 0.69 / 0.73).

The cost estimate uses the runner's 120-token guess for a json answer plus 600 reasoning tokens; real replies carry one rationale per entity, so the true spend is likely a few times higher (still well under USD 30 for 300 calls).

Effort level: the high-effort run cannot fit the authors' 12,000-token limit on 86% of documents (see params_source); if the authors' Responses-API path counts tokens differently, the S row may still have been a high-effort run - a human should compare against the released run logs if any exist in the repository.
2026-09-21: effort resolved from the released provider code (no effort field -> API default medium); medium run launched as the canonical attempt, high and low kept as sensitivity archives.

2026-09-21 20:54: the medium run stopped at its $15 cap after 145 calls ($15.25): 49 documents in file order, 48 of them with all three seeds and one with a single seed. 61 of the 145 replies (42%) were empty because the 12,000-token output limit was spent on hidden reasoning (finish_reason length). Strict-match F1 0.268 (seeds 0.272 / 0.283 / 0.249; document-resample 95% CI about 0.17-0.37) against the paper's 0.46 -> deviated, the same class as the low run (0.287 on all 100 documents, replies filled). Finishing the remaining 51 documents would cost about $17 and cannot move the class, so the cap-stopped subset stands as the canonical medium result; the effort level changes how many replies come back empty, not whether Table 1's S column is reproduced.
notes: Authors' artefacts: prompts, entity schema, guidelines and the 100 evaluation documents are all in github.com/KonWooKim/llm-guideline-moderation; PubAnnotation project ncbi-valid holds the stored annotations. The G (original guidelines) and M (moderation) columns of the same row use the same base template with data/guidelines/ncbi_disease_guidelines.txt in the guidelines slot and an agentic refinement loop respectively; only S is a single call per document and is therefore the config here.
